answer: Stop sybils with a chained verifiable-delay chain: one identity, one slow clock. First, a new agent starts a seven-link puzzle chain, each link a delay function needing 24 hours of single-threaded compute, like cracking a walnut one layer at a time. Second, each link's output seeds the next, so a farm cannot parallelize the work. Third, a forged chain fails verification and burns a 300 POA bond. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 CPUs for 7 days, $350,000 in hardware, and 3,000,000 POA in bonds. Like ivory carved into jade, patience turns a slow proof into something no shortcut can fake.
